title: Laboratory response to an infant with suspected measles vaccine associated fever and rash in Sri Lanka.
ehr_evidence: This single center, laboratory-based case investigation was carried out in NML, Department of Virolgy at MRI, SL.
summary: Laboratory investigation of a single 9-month-old infant in Sri Lanka who developed fever and rash following MMR vaccination, identifying vaccine-type measles virus and influenza A co-infection.
key_findings: Measles vaccine-type A (Edmonston-strain) virus was detected in 1 throat swab via RT-PCR and sequencing.
Measles IgM and IgG were positive at the sixth week of illness onset.
Influenza A RNA was detected in 1 throat swab at day three.
Parvovirus B19 IgM was detected in serum at the sixth week.
No evidence of human-to-human measles transmission was detected.
limitations: potential confounding from concurrent influenza A infection
limited clinical and laboratory data due to sample volume constraints
data_availability_statement: Data sharing not applicable to this article as no datasets were generated or analyzed during the current study.
